action: Mozilla's advisory names the fixed Thunderbird version; the Saudi National Cybersecurity Authority's alert encourages users to review the advisory and apply the updates.
exec: Mozilla rates the overall impact Critical, so unpatched Thunderbird mail clients are worth updating.
plain: Mozilla released a Thunderbird update with security fixes, including one rated Critical that could make a signed email appear to come from a different sender.

key_findings: Mozilla Foundation Security Advisory 2026-134 was announced on November 24, 2026, overall impact Critical.
The advisory page does not say whether any of the issues are exploited in the wild.
CVE-2026-136226 (Critical): an attacker could make Thunderbird display a different sender than the one used to verify an OpenPGP signature.
The Saudi National Cybersecurity Authority issued a Critical-severity alert for Mozilla products on 24 November.
recommendations: Update Thunderbird to the fixed version named in the advisory.

summary: Mozilla's advisory MFSA 2026-134, announced on 24 November, lists security fixes in a new Thunderbird release with an overall impact of Critical. The one Critical entry, CVE-2026-136226, could let an attacker make Thunderbird show a different sender than the one used to verify an OpenPGP signature. The page does not say whether any flaw is exploited. Saudi Arabia's NCA issued a Critical-severity alert.
title: Mozilla fixes Thunderbird flaws, including a Critical OpenPGP sender-spoofing bug (MFSA 2026-134)

validation.note: Mozilla advisory read in full; Saudi NCA alert read and points to the same advisory (not an independent report).

date_note: Date is the advisory's announcement day, 24 November, as stated on the page.
